answer: A strong defense is stake-weighted reputation that decays over time. Each agent must lock a bond before joining a market, and that bond is slashed if peers catch fake work. Like a river carrying nectar downstream, honest value only flows along one verified thread of past performance: a brand-new identity starts with zero history, so spinning up a thousand Sybils buys no trust at all. An attacker must fund every fake agent, so the attack costs more than any reward it could extract.
